newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse January turnover sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse January turnover sharply down.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange reported on Friday a sharp 24.95 percent decline in its January turnover, blaming tight liquidity of the banking sector for the plunge.
Total January turnover stood at 34.694 million dinars ($6.37 million) in 121 deals, the bourse said.
"Poor liquidity of the banking sector in the whole country, very pronounced in December, continued in January boosting demand for fresh borrowing," Natasa Bulajic of the bourse told Reuters.
Short-term securities accounted for 18.408 million dinars or 53.06 percent of the January total. The bourse traded only in companies' short-term bonds.
Giro-money transactions, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, accounted for the remaining 16.286 million dinars.
Interest rates on short-term securities ranged between an annual 221 and 474.2 percent, with maturity most frequently standing at 10-15 days.
There were no deals in central bank short-term bonds. The National Bank of Yugoslavia has not auctioned its bonds on the Podgorica-based bourse since last August, Bulajic said.
The Montenegro Stock Exchange also said it will soon start trading in commercial paper.

"There are requests to list 392 commercial papers worth 32 million dinars with maturity of 10, 15, 20 and 30 days. Those are discount securities, with 12 percent monthly interest calculated in their nominal value," the bourse said.
